items.title: Mouse study reveals magnetic nanoparticles' potential for ectopic pregnancy diagnosis and treatment
items.summary: A research team led by an Oregon State University scientist has demonstrated in a mouse model a potentially better way to care for women facing the life-threatening condition of ectopic pregnancy.

items.title: Wood beneath German lake may reveal buildings 3,000 years older than region's first farms
items.summary: Underwater archaeological investigations have been taking place in Lake Arendsee (Altmarkkreis Salzwedel) for several years. The discovery of Neolithic fish weirs, a high medieval barge (flat-bottomed cargo ship) and a late medieval dugout canoe attracted considerable attention.

items.title: Groups of genetically identical fish follow different behavioral paths as they mature
items.summary: Schooling fish have long fascinated us with their mesmerizing collective movements and seemingly perfect coordination. items.title: UV light locks radiation-detecting materials into durable, water-resistant films
items.summary: Florida State University researchers have developed a method to make a class of materials more robust and potentially easier to manufacture for advanced radiation detection devices, including those used in medical imaging and radiation therapy as well as space technologies.

items.title: Stratospheric observatory Sunrise-III reveals intricate solar magnetic structures
items.summary: A team of researchers led by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan discovered unexpectedly intricate magnetic structures above quiet-sun regions by observing the sun with the balloon-borne solar observatory Sunrise-III during its 2024 flight in Earth's stratosphere. items.title: Astronomi možda otkrili planet u nastanjivoj zoni dosad najtoplije zvijezde
items.summary: ASTRONOMI su otkrili mogućeg kandidata za planet, HD 156295 b, u nastanjivoj zoni zvijezde A-tipa. Ako se potvrdi, bit će to prvi takav planet oko najtoplije zvijezde dosad.

items.title: NASA satellite can monitor most of world's irrigation canals, study finds
items.summary: Irrigation canals form a sort of circulatory system for global agriculture. Across the world, millions of kilometers of human-made canals carry water from lakes, rivers and reservoirs downhill to farmland. items.summary: For decades, astronomers have identified collisions between two neutron stars through bursts of gamma rays that can disappear in less than two seconds. items.summary: Where did the roughly 100 species of New World blackbirds alive today originate, and how did they spread across the Americas? Dr. Axel Arango Garcia and professor Chaitanya S. items.title: Longer lives despite mitochondrial defects? Worms rely on calcium-triggered 'cages'
items.summary: If your car's engine develops a stutter, that's generally a sign that you should go to a mechanic before it stops running. items.title: Your home's energy performance is already affecting your mortgage––soon climate risk will too
items.summary: Few consumers realize that a property's poor energy rating can directly affect their ability to obtain a mortgage. In the future, flood and other climate-related risks will also play a greater role in lending decisions.

items.title: Bending nanoribbons tunes diamond's light emission without doping
items.summary: In a new Physical Review Letters study, researchers have demonstrated that bending diamond nanostructures can tune the light they emit without doping.

items.title: DNK analiza gotovo sigurno potvrdila da je Thomas Jefferson imao djecu s ropkinjom
items.summary: NOVA DNA studija, analizom vlasi kose Thomasa Jeffersona i potomaka, s 99,96% sigurnosti potvrdila je da je bivši američki predsjednik imao djecu s porobljenom ženom Sally Hemings.

items.title: AI-enhanced petitions on Change.org: More text, less success
items.summary: The change was obvious—but in the end, things stayed about the same. Cornell researchers took advantage of online petition website Change.org's gradual rollout of an artificial intelligence writing tool to gauge AI-enhanced language's impact on petition outcomes.

items.title: New click beetle species named after Dominican Republic's Indigenous Arawak people
items.summary: A new species of click beetle with a glossy and highly domed black body has been described from cloud forest sites in the mountains of the Dominican Republic and named in honor of the Arawak peoples who lived on the island before European colonization.

items.title: Research collaboration helps Gulf Coast communities plan for the unpredictable
items.summary: For communities along the Gulf Coast, hurricane season presents a recurring challenge: knowing when, where and how to evacuate before a major storm hits. items.title: Mysterious oarfish's fins inspire large underwater robot design
items.summary: When designing a large underwater robot that could swim silently to avoid startling sea creatures, roboticist Rob Shepherd considered the unusual swimming system of oarfish, the meters-long fish whose ribbon-like dorsal fin moves in waves to propel its body.

items.title: How sea squirts perceive underwater noise
items.summary: Shipping, construction work and other human activities are altering the acoustic conditions in our planet's seas. items.title: International study identifies key childhood experiences that predict happiness and well-being in adulthood
items.summary: A new study, led by the University of Nottingham and conducted across three countries, has identified a set of key childhood experiences that predict multiple measures of well-being in adulthood—including health, happiness, anxiety, life satisfaction, satisfaction with social relationships and gener

items.title: NASA, International Partners Advance Work on Space Crops
items.summary: NASA, CSA (Canadian Space Agency), and the German Aerospace Center signed a joint statement of intent to begin coordinated, preparatory work toward an Earth-based demonstrator to learn how to grow crops on the Moon.

items.title: Women leave psychology research more often than men, especially early in their careers
items.summary: Today, women are more likely than men to begin an academic career in psychology. Nevertheless, they leave research substantially more often, particularly during the first years after entering the field.

items.title: SpaceX povlači raketu i kapsulu koje koristi godinama. Zamijenit će ih golemi Starship
items.summary: NAKON povijesnog uspjeha Starshipa, SpaceX planira povući rakete Falcon 9 i letjelice Dragon. Odluka izaziva zabrinutost u svemirskoj industriji zbog nedostatka alternativa i mogućeg rasta cijena.

items.title: Antarctica's ice loss is locked in, and extra snowfall won't save it—low‑lying coastal areas elsewhere to suffer
items.summary: Sea-level rise is one of the most visible signs of climate change, one that is threatening low-lying coastal communities around the world. Today, about 1 billion people live in coastal areas; about 100 million live within 1 meter (3.3 feet) of sea level, highly exposed to coastal flooding.

items.title: Chlamydia packs DNA with lipids, revealing possible target for blocking infection
items.summary: The bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis is one of the most common causes of sexually transmitted infections worldwide.
